**201. Sponsored Research in Higher Education Institutions**

**201.1. Definition and Scope**

• Sponsored research refers to research projects funded by external agencies (government, industry, NGOs) to address specific problems or advance scientific knowledge.

• It includes collaborative research, contract research, consultancy-based studies, and innovation-driven initiatives.

**201.2. Key Objectives**

• Promote applied and interdisciplinary research aligned with societal, industrial, or national priorities.

• Build academic-industry partnerships and foster real-world problem-solving.

• Encourage capacity building among faculty, researchers, and students.

• Enable technology development, transfer, and commercialization.

**201.3. Funding Sources**

• Government agencies: DST, SERB, DBT, ICSSR, AICTE, UGC, DRDO, ISRO, ICMR.

• International bodies: World Bank, UNESCO, EU Horizon, NIH, DFID, USAID.

• Industry partners: Private corporations, start-ups, PSUs.

• Philanthropic foundations: Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation, Tata Trusts, Ford Foundation.

**201.4. Process of Sponsored Research**

• Proposal Development:

> o Identify relevant funding call.
>
> o Prepare proposal with problem statement, objectives, methodology, budget, and expected outcomes.

• Approval and Submission:

> o Submit via PI (Principal Investigator) through the institution's research cell.
>
> o Route through internal review/ethics committees if required.

• Project Execution:

> o Conduct research as per agreed deliverables and timeline.
>
> o Submit periodic progress reports and utilisation certificates.

• Closure and Outcomes:

> o Final report submission.
>
> o Publication, patenting, or technology transfer as per MoU.

**201.5. Institutional Support Systems**

• Research & Development Cell (RDC) or Sponsored Research Office (SRO).

• Grants management systems and internal audit mechanisms.

• IPR Cell to manage patents, MoUs, NDAs, etc.

• Incubation Centres and Technology Transfer Offices for commercialisation.

**201.6. Benefits to HEIs**

• Strengthens research infrastructure and lab capabilities.

• Enhances reputation and ranking in research and innovation metrics.

• Provides training and employment opportunities for research scholars.

• Generates intellectual property, prototypes, and technology solutions.

**201.7. Challenges and Mitigation**

• Delays in fund disbursement or project approval.

> o Mitigation: Strong liaison with funding agencies.

• Compliance and reporting overload.

> o Mitigation: Dedicated administrative support and training.

• Limited awareness or proposal writing skills among faculty.

> o Mitigation: Conducting workshops and mentoring schemes.

**202. ICMR (Indian Council of Medical Research) Sponsored Research in Higher Education Institutions**

**202.1. Objectives of ICMR-Sponsored Research in HEIs**

• Promote biomedical and health research across universities and medical institutions.

• Encourage evidence-based research to address national health priorities.

• Build research capacity among faculty, scholars, and students in life sciences and medicine.

• Support translational research for public health and clinical applications.

**202.2. Major Research Funding Schemes**

• Ad-hoc Research Projects:

> o Supports investigator-initiated proposals in any area of biomedical science.

• ICMR-STS (Short-Term Studentship):

> o Enables undergraduate medical/dental students to undertake short-term research projects.

• ICMR-RA (Research Associateship):

> o For post-doctoral researchers in health and allied sciences.

• ICMR Emeritus Scientist Scheme:

> o Grants for retired scientists to continue their research in HEIs.

• ICMR Junior and Senior Research Fellowships (JRF/SRF):

> o Supports full-time research scholars in medical or biomedical fields.

**202.3. Priority Research Areas**

• Communicable and Non-communicable Diseases

• Public Health and Epidemiology

• Nutrition and Reproductive Health

• Mental Health and Substance Abuse

• Genomics, Stem Cells, and Molecular Biology

• AI and Digital Health Technologies in Healthcare

**202.4. Eligible Institutions and Researchers**

• Medical colleges, universities, and life science departments in HEIs.

• Faculty members, postgraduates, and researchers from recognized institutions.

• Preference given to institutions with ethics committee registration and biomedical infrastructure.

**202.5. Funding and Support**

• Project funding for:

> o Staff (JRF/SRF/RA), consumables, equipment, and contingency expenses.
>
> o Fieldwork, data collection, analysis tools, and publication costs.

• Typical funding ranges:

> o Minor projects: ₹5–10 lakhs.
>
> o Major projects: ₹20–50 lakhs+ (depending on scope).

• Project duration: 1–3 years.

**202.6. Application Process**

• Calls announced on ICMR website: https://main.icmr.nic.in

• Submit detailed research proposal with objectives, methodology, budget, and ethical clearance.

• Institutional endorsement from Head of the Department/Institute required.

• Proposals evaluated by scientific review committees.

**202.7. Monitoring and Compliance**

• Submission of periodic progress reports, financial statements, and UCs.

• Ethics approval mandatory for human/animal studies.

• Final project completion report to include outcomes and dissemination.

**202.8. Benefits to HEIs**

• Enhances research profile in biomedical and healthcare innovation.

• Encourages student-faculty collaboration in clinical research.

• Opens doors for public health policy contributions and consultancy.

• Enables infrastructure development for medical research labs and biobanks.

**203. AICTE (All India Council for Technical Education) Sponsored Research in Higher Education Institutions**

**203.1. Objectives of AICTE-Sponsored Research in HEIs**

• Promote applied and impactful research in engineering, technology, and management.

• Strengthen research capacity and innovation ecosystem in technical institutions.

• Support faculty and student research projects aligned with national missions.

• Foster industry-academia collaboration for practical solutions and product development.

**203.2. Key Research Funding Schemes by AICTE**

• Research Promotion Scheme (RPS):

> o Funding for innovative research projects by faculty in AICTE-approved institutions.
>
> o Support for equipment, manpower, and contingencies.

• Modernisation and Removal of Obsolescence (MODROB):

> o Grants for upgrading labs with modern tools to support research and student projects.

• AICTE Doctoral Fellowship (ADF):

> o Fellowship for full-time PhD scholars in technical institutions.

• Scheme for Promoting Interests, Creativity and Ethics among Students (SPICES):

> o Supports student clubs for research, innovation, and ethical practices.

• Grant for Organizing Conference (GOC) and Seminar Grant:

> o Funding for hosting research dissemination events in HEIs.

**203.3. Eligible Institutions**

• AICTE-approved colleges and universities (Engineering, Management, Architecture, etc.).

• Institutions with NBA/NAAC accreditation are often prioritized.

• Faculty with minimum 2 years of experience in regular positions.

**203.4. Funding Coverage**

• Support for:

> o Research staff (JRF/SRF) salaries.
>
> o Equipment purchase and software tools.
>
> o Consumables, travel, publications, and contingency expenses.

• Typical funding: ₹5–25 lakhs per project.

• Duration: 1.5 to 3 years, depending on the project scope.

**203.5. Application and Review Process**

• Call for proposals released via AICTE portal (https://aicte-india.org/).

• Online submission through AICTE PRERANA or Research portals.

• Proposal components:

> o Title, background, objectives, methodology, budget, expected outcomes.

• Review by expert peer committees based on merit, relevance, and feasibility.

**203.6. Monitoring and Evaluation**

• Periodic progress reports to be submitted to AICTE.

• Mid-term and final evaluations by expert review panel.

• Submission of Utilization Certificates (UC) and final project report required.

**203.7. Benefits to HEIs**

• Enhances institutional research output and academic visibility.

• Improves eligibility for ranking, autonomy, and centre of excellence status.

• Facilitates student involvement in real-world R&D.

• Bridges the gap between theoretical knowledge and industrial practice.

**203.8. Examples of Recent AICTE-Supported Projects**

• IoT-based smart agriculture systems.

• Solar-powered cold storage design.

• AI-based traffic management solutions.

• Cybersecurity tools for rural internet networks.

**204. BARC – Bhabha Atomic Research Centre Sponsored Research in Higher Education Institutions**

**204.1. Objective of BARC-Sponsored Research in HEIs**

• Promote cutting-edge research in nuclear science, radiation technology, and related fields.

• Strengthen academia-research institute collaboration.

• Enable faculty and student involvement in nationally significant projects.

• Encourage technology development relevant to atomic energy, agriculture, environment, and health.

**204.2. Sponsored Research Schemes**

• Collaborative Research Projects in nuclear science and materials.

• Funding under DAE-BRNS (Board of Research in Nuclear Sciences):

> o BRNS funds research proposals submitted by faculty from recognized HEIs.
>
> o Emphasizes basic and applied research in atomic energy-related fields.

• DAE Young Scientist Research Award for young faculty and researchers.

**204.3. Eligible Areas for Sponsorship**

• Nuclear Physics & Engineering

• Reactor Design and Safety

• Radiation Biology and Medical Applications

• Material Science & Metallurgy

• Radioisotope Applications in Industry and Agriculture

• Environmental Radiology and Waste Management

• Computational Modelling, AI in Nuclear Research

**204.4. Funding and Support**

• Full/partial funding of research equipment, consumables, and travel.

• Provision for research staff recruitment (e.g., JRF, SRF, RA).

• Access to BARC laboratories and expertise for joint research.

• Conference travel and publication support.

**204.5. Application Process**

• Submit proposal to BRNS/DAE portal with:

> o Detailed objectives, methodology, budget, and timelines.
>
> o Endorsement from institutional head or research cell.

• Proposals reviewed by technical/scientific committees at DAE.

• Projects sanctioned based on relevance, feasibility, and impact.

**204.6. Monitoring and Evaluation**

• Periodic progress reports to BRNS.

• Mid-term review by BARC-appointed committees.

• Final technical and financial report post-project completion.

• Possibility of technology transfer or prototype testing at BARC.

**204.7. Benefits to HEIs**

• Enhances research capabilities and infrastructure.

• Encourages student involvement in national R&D.

• Improves funding prospects and research reputation.

• Opportunity to build long-term partnerships with BARC/DAE.

**204.8. Challenges**

• High expectations for scientific rigor and relevance.

• Strict adherence to safety and ethical compliance.

• Limited awareness or preparedness in proposal drafting.

**205. UGC (University Grants Commission) Sponsored Research in Higher Education Institutions**

**205.1. Objectives of UGC-Sponsored Research in HEIs**

• Promote high-quality academic research across disciplines.

• Support faculty development and innovation in teaching and learning.

• Facilitate interdisciplinary and socially relevant research.

• Strengthen research infrastructure in colleges and universities.

**205.2. Major UGC Research Funding Schemes**

• Minor Research Projects (MRP):

> o Targeted at young or early-career faculty.
>
> o Funding up to ₹3–5 lakhs.

• Major Research Projects (MaRP):

> o For senior faculty with significant experience.
>
> o Funding up to ₹10–20 lakhs depending on the discipline.

• Faculty Research Promotion Scheme (FRPS):

> o Offers research grants for publishing, fieldwork, and innovation.

• Emeritus Fellowship:

> o Support for retired but active professors to continue research.

• Dr. D.S. Kothari Post-Doctoral Fellowship:

> o Fellowship for post-PhD scholars to pursue research in HEIs.

• NET-JRF Research Funding:

> o Junior Research Fellowship provided to NET-qualified candidates.

**205.3. Eligible Institutions and Researchers**

• Central, state, and deemed universities recognized under Section 2(f) and 12(B) of the UGC Act.

• Autonomous colleges and NAAC-accredited institutions.

• Full-time faculty members with a valid teaching position.

**205.4. Funding Coverage**

• Manpower: JRF/SRF/RA positions.

• Contingency: Fieldwork, travel, publication, equipment.

• Institutional overheads.

• Duration: Typically 2–3 years.

**205.5. Application Process**

• Calls for proposals announced on the UGC official website.

• Proposal must include:

> o Research objectives, rationale, methodology.
>
> o Budget estimate, outcomes, and timeline.

• Submission through HEI's Research Cell or Principal Investigator.

• Proposals are evaluated by subject expert committees.

**205.6. Monitoring and Reporting**

• Annual and final reports to be submitted to UGC.

• Financial audit and utilization certificate (UC) are mandatory.

• Mid-term evaluation in long-duration projects.

**205.7. Key Benefits to HEIs**

• Enhances institutional research culture and reputation.

• Builds research capacity among young faculty and students.

• Helps HEIs qualify for autonomy, ranking, and NAAC/NERF recognition.

• Promotes knowledge dissemination through publications and patents.

**205.8. Challenges and Mitigation**

• Delayed fund disbursement – streamlined by online portals.

• Lack of awareness – can be mitigated through workshops/webinars.

• Proposal quality – improved via internal peer reviews before submission.

**206. Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) Sponsored Research in Higher Education Institutions**

**206.1. Objectives of MeitY-Sponsored Research in HEIs**

• Promote cutting-edge R&D in electronics, IT, and emerging technologies.

• Foster industry-academia collaboration for innovation and product development.

• Build skilled human resources in AI, cybersecurity, quantum computing, etc.

• Support Make in India and Digital India goals through indigenous research.

**206.2. Major Research Support Schemes**

• R&D in Emerging Areas Scheme:

> o AI, IoT, Blockchain, 5G, Quantum Technologies, Robotics, and ESDM.

• Visvesvaraya PhD Scheme:

> o Fellowship and contingency grants for PhD students in electronics and IT.

• Technology Incubation and Development of Entrepreneurs (TIDE 2.0):

> o Funding for HEI-based startups and tech incubators.

• Centres of Excellence (CoEs) in academic institutions:

> o AI, NLP, FinTech, Cybersecurity, and Blockchain.

**206.3. Eligible Institutions**

• Centrally funded technical institutions (IITs, NITs, IIITs).

• State universities and reputed private engineering colleges.

• Institutions having active R&D cells and incubation centres.

**206.4. Funding and Support**

• Financial support for:

> o Manpower (JRF, SRF, RA)
>
> o Equipment and software licenses
>
> o Patent filing and prototype development
>
> o Conferences and dissemination

• Duration of most projects: 1.5 to 3 years.

**206.5. Application and Approval Process**

• Call for proposals published on the MeitY website or through institutional outreach.

• Proposal must include:

> o Problem statement, objectives, methodology
>
> o Budget justification, expected outcomes
>
> o Institutional endorsement

• Reviewed by MeitY-appointed expert committees.

• Monitoring through periodic reporting and on-site reviews.

**206.6. Key Outcomes Expected**

• Development of IPRs, prototypes, or commercial-ready technologies.

• Publications in reputed journals and conferences.

• Training of students and faculty in niche technology domains.

• Enhancement of India's self-reliance in critical technology areas.

**206.7. Recent Examples of Sponsored Projects**

• CoE in AI at IIT Kharagpur, NLP CoE at IIIT Hyderabad.

• Quantum Computing research at IIT Madras, IISc Bengaluru.

• Cyber Forensics initiatives at NIELIT and C-DAC in collaboration with HEIs.

**206.8. Institutional Benefits**

• Strengthens institutional R&D infrastructure and innovation ecosystem.

• Enhances visibility in national digital missions.

• Increases opportunities for faculty and student collaboration with MeitY and industry.

**207. DST (Department of Science and Technology) Sponsored Research in Higher Education Institutions**

The Department of Science and Technology (DST) is a key government agency under the Ministry of Science and Technology, Government of India. Established in 1971, DST is responsible for promoting new areas of science and technology and coordinating scientific research activities across India.

**207.1. Department of Science and Technology (DST): Overview**

• Founded: 3 May 1971

• Headquarters: Technology Bhawan, New Mehrauli Road, New Delhi

• Ministry: Ministry of Science and Technology, Government of India

• Primary Role: Formulation and implementation of policies for scientific research, technology development, and innovation.

**207.2. Key Objectives of DST**

1\. Promote Scientific Research and Development (R&D)

2\. Develop Science and Technology Infrastructure

3\. Support Innovation and Technology Commercialization

4\. Encourage International Scientific Cooperation

5\. Popularize Science Among the Public and Youth

6\. Fund Capacity Building Programs in S&T

**207.3. Major Divisions and Programs of DST**

• Science and Engineering Research Board (SERB)

• Technology Development Program (TDP)

• Innovation and Startup Programs (NIDHI, PRISM)

• Science for Equity, Empowerment and Development (SEED)

• Women Scientists Program (WOS-A/B/C)

• FIST Program (Fund for Improvement of S&T Infrastructure)

• INSPIRE Program (Innovation in Science Pursuit for Inspired Research)

• National Mission on Interdisciplinary Cyber-Physical Systems (NM-ICPS)

• Climate Change and Clean Energy Research

**207.4. Flagship Programs and Initiatives**

• Key Focus Areas

• Infrastructure funding for universities and research institutions

• Attracts young talent to science through fellowships and scholarships

• Promotes research in AI, robotics, IoT, etc.

• Supports adaptation and mitigation technologies

1\. INSPIRE (Innovation in Science Pursuit for Inspired Research)

• Scholarships and fellowships for school to post-doctoral levels.

• Includes *INSPIRE Awards*, *Scholarship for Higher Education (SHE)*, and *INSPIRE Faculty Scheme*.

2\. FIST (Fund for Improvement of S&T Infrastructure)

• Supports upgrading laboratories and research infrastructure in academic institutions.

3\. NIDHI (National Initiative for Developing and Harnessing Innovations)

• Supports innovators and early-stage startups through:

> o PRAYAS, Entrepreneur-in-Residence, Seed Support System, and Technology Business Incubators (TBIs).

4\. Women Scientists Scheme (WOS-A/B/C)

• Promotes participation of women in science and technology through research grants and fellowships.

5\. TARE (Teacher Associateship for Research Excellence)

• Helps faculty from colleges and universities to collaborate with premier research institutes.

**207.5. International Cooperation**

DST fosters global S&T cooperation through bilateral and multilateral partnerships with countries such as:

• USA (NSF), Germany (DFG), UK (UKRI), France (CNRS), Russia, Japan, Australia, South Korea, and others.

• Engages in global platforms like BRICS, ASEAN, and UNESCO.

**207.6. Budget and Funding**

DST manages a significant portion of India's public science funding. It supports:

• R&D institutions

• Universities and colleges

• Individual researchers

• Startups and MSMEs

• S&T infrastructure development

**207.7. How to Apply for DST Funding?**

1\. Visit the official DST portal: https://dst.gov.in

2\. Check calls for proposals under schemes like SERB, INSPIRE, FIST, etc.

3\. Submit online applications via:

> o SERB online portal: https://www.serbonline.in
>
> o INSPIRE portal: https://www.online-inspire.gov.in

**207.8. Notable DST-Affiliated Institutions**

• SERB – Science and Engineering Research Board

• TIFAC – Technology Information Forecasting and Assessment Council

• NCSTC – National Council for Science & Technology Communication

• Vigyan Prasar – Science Communication and Outreach

• SAMEER, NCPOR, NIF, ARIES, IASST, etc.

**207.9. Major Research Funding Schemes**

• Science and Engineering Research Board (SERB):

> o Core Research Grant (CRG) – Supports individual and team research in frontier science.
>
> o Startup Research Grant (SRG) – For early-career faculty starting independent research.
>
> o SUPRA – Funding for high-risk, high-reward research.

• Fund for Improvement of S&T Infrastructure (FIST):

> o Strengthens departmental infrastructure in HEIs.

• Promotion of University Research and Scientific Excellence (PURSE):

> o Supports top-performing universities based on research output.

• Innovation in Science Pursuit for Inspired Research (INSPIRE):

> o Offers fellowships and awards for students and faculty in basic sciences.

• Technology Interventions for Tribal Empowerment (TITE) and SEED Division:

> o Promote socio-economic development through S&T.

**207.10. Priority Research Areas**

• Physical and Chemical Sciences

• Mathematical and Computational Sciences

• Life Sciences and Biotechnology

• Climate Change, Renewable Energy, and Water Resources

• Artificial Intelligence, Materials Science, and Quantum Technologies

**207.11. Eligible Institutions**

• Recognized universities, IITs, NITs, IISERs, and autonomous colleges.

• NAAC/NBA-accredited institutions or those under Section 12(B) of the UGC Act.

• Faculty with a proven track record or emerging researchers.

**207.12. Funding and Support**

• Covers:

> o Research fellowships (JRF/SRF/RA) and technical staff
>
> o Equipment, software, consumables
>
> o Travel, publication, and contingency

• Duration: Usually 3 years (can vary by scheme).

• Funding amount: ₹15 lakhs to ₹1 crore+, depending on the scheme.

**207.13. Application Process**

• Online submission via SERB (**https://www.serbonline.in**) or DST portals.

• Proposal must include:

> o Title, background, objectives, methodology, expected outcomes.
>
> o Budget breakdown and institutional endorsement.

• Reviewed by peer review committees and technical experts.

**207.14. Monitoring and Reporting**

• Annual progress reports, utilization certificates, and technical review meetings.

• Final reports must detail outcomes, publications, patents, or technology development.

**207.15. Outcomes and Expectations**

• Generation of research papers, patents, or commercial products.

• Development of human capital and research leadership.

• Contribution to national science missions and societal impact.

• Recognition through awards (e.g., National Awards, Young Scientist Awards).

**207.16. Institutional Benefits**

• Builds reputation in national and global research networks.

• Enables creation of Centres of Excellence and incubation ecosystems.

• Enhances potential to attract further funding and international collaborations.

**208. CSIR (Council of Scientific and Industrial Research) Sponsored Research in Higher Education Institutions**

**208.1. Overview**

• Established: September 26, 1942

• Headquarters: New Delhi, India

• Governing Body: Ministry of Science and Technology, Government of India

• Status: Autonomous body under the Societies Registration Act, 1860

**208.2. Mission and Objectives**

CSIR's mission is to:

• Promote scientific knowledge, applied research, and industrial development

• Translate science into technology and innovate for national development

• Develop cutting-edge technologies in diverse fields for industry and societal benefit

**208.3. Key Areas of Research**

CSIR covers a broad spectrum of research disciplines, including:

| **Discipline**                | **Focus**                                                |
|-------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------|
| Aerospace                     | Indigenous aircraft, UAVs, aerospace materials           |
| Chemical Sciences             | Drug discovery, catalysis, organic synthesis             |
| Biological Sciences           | Genomics, biotech, healthcare                            |
| Engineering & Materials       | Advanced materials, MEMS, smart materials                |
| Environmental Science         | Pollution control, climate change, renewable energy      |
| Agriculture & Food Technology | Crop improvement, food preservation                      |
| Water & Waste Management      | Clean water, desalination, industrial effluent treatment |
| Energy                        | Green hydrogen, solar energy, batteries, fuel cells      |
| Mining and Earth Sciences     | Geo-surveys, resource mapping, mining technologies       |

| CSIR-NAL     | Aerospace R&D                     | Bengaluru     |
| CSIR-CIMFR   | Mining and Fuel                   | Dhanbad       |
| CSIR-NEERI   | Environmental Engineering         | Nagpur        |
| CSIR-CCMB    | Cellular and Molecular Biology    | Hyderabad     |
| CSIR-IICB    | Chemical Biology & Drug Discovery | Kolkata       |
| CSIR-CSIO    | Instrumentation                   | Chandigarh    |
| CSIR-IIP     | Petroleum                         | Dehradun      |
| CSIR-CMERI   | Mechanical Engineering            | Durgapur      |
| CSIR-NCL     | Chemical Research                 | Pune          |

There are 37 national laboratories under CSIR, each focused on specific scientific and industrial domains.

**208.5. Major Programs and Contributions**

• **Drug Development:** CSIR labs helped develop anti-COVID drug 2-DG, Artemisinin, and repurposed drugs.

• **Green Hydrogen Mission:** Developing indigenous electrolyzer and hydrogen storage technologies.

• **CSIR-Tech Led Startups:** Supports technology incubation and industry partnerships.

• **CSIR Aroma and Phytopharma Mission:** Promotes cultivation and processing of medicinal and aromatic plants.

• **CSIR-800 Program:** Science and tech for the benefit of underprivileged populations.

• **CSIR Integrated Skill Initiative:** Skilling youth in advanced scientific and technical areas.

**208.6. Opportunities for Students and Researchers**

• **CSIR-UGC NET:** For Junior Research Fellowship (JRF) and Lectureship in Science subjects.

• **CSIR-SRF and RA:** Fellowships for doctoral and postdoctoral researchers.

• **CSIR-TG (Technology Generation Grants):** For lab-to-industry research translation.

• **CSIR Innovation Awards for School Children (CIASC):** Annual awards to promote innovation.

**208.7. Collaborations**

CSIR collaborates with:

• Indian academic institutions (IITs, IISc, universities)

• Government agencies (ISRO, DRDO, DST, DBT)

• International organizations (UNESCO, EU, MIT, Max Planck Institutes)

**208.8. Impact and Achievements**

• Developed India's first synthetic drug: Methaqualone

• Developed Swaraj tractor, Saras aircraft, and EVM technology

• Helped India become self-reliant in generic pharmaceuticals and generic agrochemicals

• Pioneered research in genomics, robotics, solar energy, and corrosion science

**208.9. Major Research Funding Schemes**

• CSIR-EMR (Extra Mural Research) Scheme:

> o Core research support to faculty in HEIs for innovative projects.

• CSIR JRF/SRF/RA Fellowships:

> o For postgraduate and doctoral students in science and engineering.

• CSIR-Industry Sponsored Projects:

> o Collaborative projects involving academia and industry for translational research.

• CSIR Innovation Award for School Children (CIASC):

> o Encourages innovation culture from a young age and bridges it with HEIs later.

**208.10. Priority Research Areas**

• Chemical, Physical, and Biological Sciences

• Engineering Sciences and Materials

• Environmental Science, Water Purification, and Sustainability

• Biotechnology and Genomics

• Pharmaceutical Sciences and Drug Development

• Renewable Energy, Nanotechnology, and Smart Materials

**208.11. Eligible Institutions and Researchers**

• Recognized universities, technical institutes, and affiliated colleges.

• Faculty with proven expertise or early-career researchers in science and engineering.

• Preference for interdisciplinary, innovative, and industrially relevant projects.

**208.12. Funding and Support**

• Coverage includes:

> o Manpower (JRF/SRF/RA)
>
> o Equipment, consumables, and testing
>
> o Travel, contingency, publication, and overhead charges

• Typical duration: 2–3 years.

• Funding amount: ₹15–30 lakhs depending on project scope.

**208.13. Application and Approval Process**

• Proposal submission through CSIR-EMR online portal.

• Proposal must detail:

> o Title, objectives, methodology, budget, expected impact.
>
> o Bio-data of PI and institutional endorsement.

• Evaluated by peer review panels and CSIR technical committees.

**208.14. Monitoring and Evaluation**

• Progress reports submitted annually or bi-annually.

• Mid-term review meetings with domain experts.

• Final technical and financial report with research outcomes.

**208.15. Key Outcomes Expected**

• Research publications in peer-reviewed journals.

• Patents, prototypes, and industrial applications.

• Technology transfer to industry or government bodies.

• Capacity building in R&D through training and mentorship.

**208.16. Institutional Benefits**

• Builds long-term collaboration with CSIR labs and scientists.

• Enhances infrastructure and faculty research profiles.

• Improves funding competitiveness for other national and international grants.

• Encourages student involvement in applied science projects.

**209. TDB (Technology Development Board) Sponsored Research in Higher Education Institutions**

**209.1. Objectives of TDB-Sponsored Research in HEIs**

• Support commercialization of indigenous technologies developed in academic and R&D institutions.

• Promote translational research and technology transfer from lab to market.

• Enable industry-academia collaboration for product-oriented innovations.

• Boost entrepreneurship, start-ups, and tech-based enterprises from HEIs.

**209.2. About TDB**

• TDB is a statutory body under the Department of Science and Technology (DST), Government of India.

• Established in 1996 to facilitate financial assistance for technology development and commercialization.

• Focuses on public-private partnership (PPP) models for applied innovation.

**209.3. Types of Support for HEIs**

• Financial Assistance for Commercialization Projects:

> o Jointly submitted by HEIs and industry/start-ups.
>
> o HEIs act as technology developers or knowledge partners.

• Support for Academia-Industry Joint Ventures:

> o For scaling up of prototype to production level innovations.

• Support to HEI-Linked Startups & Spin-offs:

> o Early-stage start-ups incubated in university innovation centres are eligible.

**209.4. Priority Areas of Funding**

• Biotechnology, Healthcare, and Pharma

• Agritech and Food Processing

• Advanced Materials and Manufacturing

• Clean Energy and Waste Management

• Electronics, IoT, and AI-enabled Devices

• Environment and Climate Technologies

**209.5. Eligibility Criteria**

• Projects must have:

> o A working prototype or proven proof-of-concept developed in the HEI.
>
> o A clear commercialisation plan and industrial partner.

• HEIs can apply:

> o Independently (if planning to license/transfer IP).
>
> o Jointly with an industry/start-up partner.

**209.6. Funding Model**

• Debt or soft loan support, equity participation, or grant-in-aid (in select cases).

• Up to 50% of the total project cost can be funded.

• Repayment is flexible and based on royalty or revenue sharing.

• Project duration: Typically 1.5 to 3 years.

**209.7. Application Process**

• Proposal submission via TDB portal or by email during open calls.

• Requirements:

> o Detailed project report, technology validation, and business plan.
>
> o MoU or agreement between HEI and industrial/start-up partner.

• Evaluation by technical and financial expert committees.

**209.8. Monitoring and Compliance**

• Submission of quarterly progress reports (technical and financial).

• Review meetings with TDB officials and external evaluators.

• Compliance with IPR sharing, licensing, and revenue terms agreed upon.

**209.9. Outcomes and Expectations**

• Commercial-ready products, services, or processes with market deployment.

• Enhanced technology transfer from HEIs to industry.

• Creation of start-ups or licensing opportunities.

• Generation of patents, IPR, and public-private collaboration models.

**209.10. Institutional Benefits**

• Positioning of HEIs as innovation and entrepreneurship hubs.

• Long-term revenue through licensing and royalty sharing.

• Strengthens startup ecosystem and incubation success rate.

• Builds industry trust in academic research and development.

**210. DSIR (Department of Scientific and Industrial Research) Sponsored Research in Higher Education Institutions**

**210.1. Objectives of DSIR-Sponsored Research in HEIs**

• Promote industry-oriented scientific research and innovation in academia.

• Foster academia-industry collaboration for applied research and technology development.

• Encourage commercialisation of research outcomes in HEIs.

• Support capacity building and technology incubation in science and engineering domains.

**210.2. Major Research Support Schemes**

• Collaborative Research Schemes (CRS):

> o Joint R&D projects between HEIs and industry partners.

• Industrial R&D Promotion Programme (IRDPP):

> o Encourages HEIs to engage in industry-relevant research and technology solutions.

• Technopreneur Promotion Programme (TePP) (Now merged under NIDHI-TBI with DST):

> o Supports innovation-led entrepreneurship through HEIs and incubators.

• Technology Development and Innovation Programme (TDIP):

> o Funds lab-to-market transition of technologies developed in HEIs.

• Recognition of R&D Units:

> o Facilitates research partnerships between recognised academic labs and industries.

**210.3. Priority Research Areas**

• Advanced Manufacturing and Materials

• Automation, Robotics, and IoT

• Green Energy and Environmental Technologies

• Biotech for Industry and Process Engineering

• Waste to Wealth, Water Purification, and Circular Economy

• S&T for MSME Development and Industrial Sustainability

**210.4. Eligible Institutions**

• Public and private universities, engineering colleges, and technical institutes.

• Must be recognized under UGC/AICTE with active research cells or incubation centres.

• Preference to institutions with existing collaborations with industry or MSMEs.

**210.5. Funding and Support**

• Funding includes:

> o Manpower (JRF/SRF/RA) for project execution
>
> o R&D equipment, prototyping, and testing support
>
> o Travel, publication, pilot production costs
>
> o Partial support for commercialization (in collaboration with industry)

• Typical funding: ₹10 lakhs to ₹1 crore depending on project scope and industry involvement.

• Duration: Usually 1.5 to 3 years

**210.6. Application Process**

• Proposal submission via DSIR online portals or email when calls are announced.

• Proposal components:

> o Problem statement, objectives, industrial relevance, budget, methodology.
>
> o MoU or commitment letter from industry collaborator.

• Review by technical experts from DSIR and industrial bodies.

**210.7. Monitoring and Compliance**

• Periodic submission of progress reports and financial statements.

• Project reviews via site visits or virtual meetings with DSIR officials.

• Final project report and transfer of results/IP if applicable.

**210.8. Expected Outcomes**

• Development of commercial prototypes, industrial solutions, or new technologies.

• Industry-ready graduates trained in applied R&D.

• Generation of IPR, publications, and proof-of-concept demonstrations.

• Facilitation of start-ups and spin-offs within HEIs.

**210.9. Institutional Benefits**

• Strengthens the institution's role in industry-driven innovation ecosystems.

• Enhances potential to become Technology Business Incubators (TBIs) or R&D centres of excellence.

• Builds long-term institution-industry-government linkages.

• Contributes to national innovation and industrial competitiveness goals.

**211. ICAR (Indian Council of Agricultural Research) Sponsored Research in Higher Education Institutions**

**211.1. Objectives of ICAR-Sponsored Research in HEIs**

• Promote agricultural innovation, sustainability, and food security through R&D.

• Support faculty and student research in agriculture and allied sectors.

• Strengthen linkages between academic institutions, farmers, and industry.

• Address national priorities in agriculture, climate resilience, and rural development.

**211.2. Major Research Funding Schemes**

• National Agricultural Science Fund (NASF):

> o Supports frontier and high-impact agricultural research across disciplines.

• All India Coordinated Research Projects (AICRP):

> o Multi-institutional long-term research in thematic areas like crops, soil, livestock, and fisheries.

• Krishi Vigyan Kendras (KVKs):

> o Promote research-based extension activities through HEI-based agricultural outreach.

• Extramural Research Projects:

> o Competitive grants for universities and colleges to conduct innovative agricultural studies.

• NICRA (National Innovations on Climate Resilient Agriculture):

> o Focus on climate adaptation, crop modeling, and sustainable farming practices.

**211.3. Priority Research Areas**

• Crop Improvement and Genomics

• Soil Science and Water Management

• Animal Sciences, Fisheries, and Dairy Technology

• Agricultural Engineering and Farm Mechanization

• Agri-Biotechnology, Bioinformatics, and Precision Farming

• Post-Harvest Technology, Food Processing, and Storage

• Agri-Economics, Rural Development, and Extension Education

**211.4. Eligible Institutions**

• State Agricultural Universities (SAUs)

• ICAR-affiliated Deemed Universities

• AICTE/UGC-approved HEIs with agriculture or life sciences departments

• Colleges of Agriculture, Horticulture, Forestry, Veterinary Sciences, etc.

**211.5. Funding and Support**

• Includes:

> o Research manpower (JRF/SRF/RA)
>
> o Equipment, field inputs, and lab infrastructure
>
> o Contingency, publication, and travel
>
> o Farm trials and farmer engagement activities

• Duration: 2 to 5 years

• Funding range: ₹20 lakhs to ₹2 crores (depending on project scope)

**211.6. Application Process**

• Calls issued via ICAR's website or through individual directorates and divisions.

• Proposal must include:

> o Detailed technical write-up, objectives, methodology, outcomes
>
> o Budget justification and institutional support letter

• Reviewed by discipline-specific committees and domain experts

**211.7. Monitoring and Evaluation**

• Submission of quarterly/annual technical and financial reports

• Field visits and review workshops conducted by ICAR scientists

• Final project evaluation includes technology transfer outcomes, publications, and policy implications

**211.8. Expected Outcomes**

• Development of improved crop varieties, farm tools, or livestock breeds

• Extension materials, mobile apps, or ICT tools for farmers

• Patents, publications, and models for scalability

• Strengthened student training and agri-tech capacity building

**211.9. Institutional Benefits**

• Enhanced status as centres of excellence or regional research hubs

• Qualification for future ICAR mega-projects

• Opportunity to contribute to national food and nutrition security

• Engagement in farmer participatory research and rural transformation

**212. DRDO (Defence Research and Development Organisation) Sponsored Research in Higher Education Institutions**

**212.1. Introduction**

The Defence Research and Development Organization (DRDO) is India's premier R&D agency responsible for developing cutting-edge technologies for the Indian armed forces. It operates under the Ministry of Defence, Government of India.

• Established: 1958

• Headquarters: DRDO Bhavan, New Delhi

• Motto: *“Balasya Mulam Vigyanam”* (Strength's Origin is in Science)

**212.2. Objectives and Mandate**

• Design, develop, and produce defense systems and dual-use technologies

• Promote self-reliance in defense technology

• Transfer technology to Indian industries and PSUs

• Strengthen the Indian military through indigenous innovations

**212.3. Major Areas of R&D**

| Aeronautics           | UAVs, fighters (Tejas), airframes                  |

| Electronics & Warfare | Radars, jammers, EW systems                        |
| Life Sciences         | High-altitude medicine, nutrition, protective gear |
| Materials             | Stealth coatings, composites, ceramics             |
| Cyber & AI            | Defense-grade AI, autonomous systems               |
| Missile Systems       | Agni, Prithvi, Akash, Nag, BrahMos                 |

DRDO operates through a network of over 50 laboratories and establishments, each specializing in different areas of defense R&D.
